sources.entry: responses - A utility library for mocking out the requests Python library.

summary.one_liner: Responses is a Python utility library for mocking out the requests library so tests can register fake HTTP responses instead of hitting real servers.
keywords: stop real http calls in tests
summary.what_it_does: Lets you register mock responses for requests calls by method and URL, either by passing a Response object or direct arguments, and by using decorators, shortcuts like responses.get/post, or a context manager. Unmatched requests raise a ConnectionError. It provides matchers for JSON and URL-encoded bodies, query parameters or query strings, request kwargs, multipart/form-data, headers, and fragment identifiers, plus support for custom matchers. Dynamic responses can be produced with callbacks, including regex URL matching. It can assert call counts and inspect calls, and supports ordered registries for sequence-dependent responses, passthrough to real servers, and a beta recorder that saves real responses to YAML and replays them.
use_cases: mock a third-party API in unit tests
simulate HTTP error codes like 404 or 500
verify request headers, bodies, or query params sent by code
test retry logic with a sequence of responses
record real API responses to a YAML file for later replay
how_to_run: import responses and decorate a test function with @responses.activate
call responses.get/post/put(url, json=..., status=...) to register mock responses
run requests calls in the test as usual and assert on the results
notable: Only mocks the requests library; calls made through other HTTP clients are not covered by the README
Ordered registry makes responses depend on call order, useful for retry tests
Beta recorder saves real responses to YAML and can replay them into the registry
Optional pytest fixture via the separate pytest-responses package
caveats: Requires Python 3.8 or newer and requests 2.30.0 or newer
Recording and replay features are marked BETA and their API may change
Several arguments are deprecated (match_querystring, stream on Response) with migration paths given
